description:
The food.gdt dataset is open in Gretl. It contains real household survey data with two variables: 'food_exp' (weekly food expenditure in dollars) and 'income' (weekly income in $100 units) for 40 households.

First, run an OLS regression of food_exp on income (Model > Ordinary Least Squares, with food_exp as dependent and income as regressor, click OK). Then, in the OLS results window, test for heteroskedasticity using White's test: go to Tests > Heteroskedasticity > White's test. After the test results appear showing the White test statistic and p-value, save the results to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/white_test_results.txt using File > Save to file in the results window.

metadata.data_source: Hill, Griffiths, Lim - Principles of Econometrics 5th ed, household survey data
